record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Characterize exactly which Nijenhuis operators admit at least one geodesically compatible metric, and for each such operator describe all metrics geodesically compatible with it, especially near singular points and in non-Riemannian signature.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Which Nijenhuis operators admit at least one geodesically compatible metric g? Given L, describe all the metrics geodesically compatible with it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge 2$ and let $L:TM\to TM$ be a (1,1)-tensor field (an operator field). The Nijenhuis torsion of $L$ is the (1,2)-tensor
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)=L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY],\qquad X,Y\in\mathfrak{X}(M),$$
and $L$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if $\mathcal{N}_L\equiv 0$.

A pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ (of arbitrary signature) is said to be geodesically compatible with $L$ if:
(i) $L$ is $g$-self-adjoint, i.e. $g(LX,Y)=g(X,LY)$ for all $X,Y$; and
(ii) the (unparametrised) geodesics of $g$ coincide with the (unparametrised) geodesics of the metric $g_L$ defined by $g_L(X,Y)=g(LX,Y)\cdot(\det L)^{-1}$ (equivalently, $g$ and $g_L$ are geodesically equivalent in the classical Levi-Civita/Beltrami sense).

Solve the following two questions:

(a) Give a complete characterisation of those Nijenhuis operators $L$ on $M$ which admit at least one geodesically compatible pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$.

(b) For each Nijenhuis operator $L$ as in (a), describe explicitly the set of all pseudo-Riemannian metrics $g$ geodesically compatible with $L$. The description must be valid in arbitrary signature and must also cover neighbourhoods of singular points of $L$ (points where the algebraic type of $L$ — its eigenvalue multiplicities and Jordan block structure — degenerates).
artifact.category_tag: Nijenhuis operators and geodesically compatible metrics
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is partially solved. For gl-regular Nijenhuis operators (in particular diagonalisable gl-regular ones), the set of geodesically compatible metrics has been fully described in recent work of Bolsinov, Konyaev and Matveev (Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V, 2023/2024) and Bolsinov (Sb. Math. 216:5, 2025), where existence is characterised via a PDE system whose integrability is equivalent to vanishing Nijenhuis torsion, and all compatible metrics form a Sinjukov–Topalov-type hierarchy. A general characterisation valid at singular (non-gl-regular) points and in arbitrary signature is not yet available.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V: geodesically equivalent metrics and finite-dimensional reductions of certain integrable quasilinear systems
status_evidence.snippet: All metrics geodesically compatible with a gl-regular Nijenhuis operator L can be described; for diagonalisable gl-regular L every symmetry has the form f(L), so compatible metrics form a generalised Sinjukov–Topalov hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Complete description is known in the gl-regular case, characterising existence and listing all compatible metrics.

status_evidence.title: A. V. Bolsinov, Geodesically equivalent metrics and Nijenhuis geometry, Sb. Math. 216:5 (2025), 583–607
status_evidence.snippet: Geodesically equivalent metrics, Nijenhuis operators, geodesic flows, symmetries, conservation laws.
status_evidence.claim: Recent paper develops the characterisation of geodesically compatible metrics via Nijenhuis geometry.
